newsitem.title: FINLAND: ENSO SAYS HAS WOOD PRICE DEAL.
newsitem.headline: ENSO SAYS HAS WOOD PRICE DEAL.

text.p: Finland's second largest forest industry group Enso Oy and private forest owners have reached agreement on wood prices for the period April 2 to end-January 1998, an Enso official said on Wednesday.

Logwood prices can rise by four to five percent compared to the national average last autumn, pulpwood prices would be unchanged and spruce pulpwood would rise about two percent, Enso forest director Voitto Polkki told Reuters by telephone.
"Considering the weak pulp market situation, the pulpwood price is still too high, but this is a negotiation result," Polkki said.
"But it does make trade possible and we are pleased that there is agreement," he added.
Finland's largest forest industry group UPM-Kymmene announced a similar deal on March 20.
